# elves_config_rule (Resource)

Includes or excludes one rule for a list of configurations. Configuration rules apply to every Mac using the configuration, after the default rules and before SCIM group, SCIM user and Mac rules. Only the listed configurations are managed: other configurations that have the same rule (set in the UI or by another resource) are left alone.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Block an app on the engineering and design configurations
resource "elves_config_rule" "block_tool" {
  rule_id    = elves_rule.blocked_tool.id
  action     = "include"
  config_ids = [2, 3]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `config_ids` (Set of Number) Required. IDs of the configurations, as shown on the Elves Configurations page.
- `rule_id` (Number) Required. ID of the rule to assign, for example `elves_rule.example.id`. Changing it replaces the assignment.

### Optional

- `action` (String) Optional. `include` adds the rule. `exclude` takes it away when an earlier level adds it: rules are applied as default rules, then the configuration, then SCIM groups, then the SCIM user, then the Mac itself. Defaults to `include`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the assignment, `<rule_id>/<action>`. Used for import, which brings in every configuration that has the rule with that action.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <rule_id>/<action>. Every configuration that has the rule with that
# action is imported.
terraform import elves_config_rule.example 68/include
```
